summary: Keeping, breeding, and selling pet roof rats is legal in New York — both statewide and in New York City. The state classifies Rattus rattus as 'unprotected wildlife,' which may be possessed and sold without restriction (ECL §11-0917(2)); it is not a prohibited 'wild animal' and not on the invasive-species list. NYC's Health Code bans only 'large rodents,' so small pet rats are allowed (a Class P pet-shop permit is needed only for commercial retail). Bringing a rat into NY from another state needs a 30-day vet health certificate; international movement is federally restricted.

keep.why: New York classifies Rattus rattus as 'unprotected wildlife,' which ECL §11-0917(2) says 'may be possessed, transported, bought and sold without restriction.' It is not a prohibited 'wild animal' (ECL §11-0512 / §11-0103(6)(e) lists primates, big cats, canids, bears, venomous reptiles, crocodilians — not rodents) and is not on the state invasive-species list (6 NYCRR Part 575). New York CITY allows it too: the NYC Health Code (Art. 161.01(b)(14)) bans only 'large rodents' (beaver, capybara, prairie dog, porcupine, etc.); small domestic rats are permitted.
keep.governing_law: NY Envtl. Conservation Law §11-0917(2) (unprotected wildlife) & §11-0512/§11-0103(6) (wild-animal pet ban — rodents excluded); NYC Health Code art. 161.01.

breed.why: No New York breeder license for rodents — the 'Pet Dealer' law (Agriculture & Markets Law Art. 26-A, §400) defines 'animal' as only dogs and cats, so breeding rats at any volume is outside it; only the general anti-cruelty rules apply. In NYC, hobby breeding is fine, but sanitation/nuisance rules (odor, escapes) apply.
breed.governing_law: NY Agric. & Markets Law Art. 26-A §400 (Pet Dealer — dogs/cats only); NYC Health Code §161.03 (nuisance).

sell_give.why: Statewide, selling roof rats is legal — a retailer must just give buyers written/digital care instructions for 'small animals' (which the law lists as including rats), per General Business Law §391-t. In New York CITY, a commercial retail seller needs a Class P 'Pet Shop' permit (NYCHC §161.09); NYC's Local Law 132 (2024) banned the retail sale of dogs, cats, guinea pigs and rabbits, but rats remain sellable. Giving rats away or private/face-to-face placement needs no permit. (Federal USDA licensing applies to wholesale/sight-unseen sales — see United States.)
sell_give.governing_law: NY Gen. Bus. Law §391-t (care instructions); NYC Health Code §161.09 & ch. 5 (Class P pet-shop permit; Local Law 132/2024).

transport.why: Within New York, no permit is required. Bringing a rat INTO New York from another state requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (health certificate) issued within 30 days (1CRR-NY 67.2); no rabies vaccine is required for rodents, and enforcement against a private owner with a single pet is reportedly minimal. International import/export is restricted at the federal level (USFWS Form 3-177; CDC African-rodent ban) — see United States.
transport.governing_law: 1CRR-NY 67.2 (companion-animal import CVI); federal USFWS 50 CFR 14.4 / CDC 42 CFR 71.56.

restrictions.summary: In New York CITY, a commercial retail seller of rats needs a Class P 'Pet Shop' permit from DOHMH (facility inspections; integrated pest management). Rats remain legally sellable in NYC even after Local Law 132 (2024) banned retail sale of dogs/cats/guinea pigs/rabbits. Private/face-to-face placement and giveaways need no permit.
steps: If running an NYC retail storefront, obtain a DOHMH Class P pet-shop permit

forms.name: NYC Health Code Ch. 5 — Pet Shops

restrictions.summary: Statewide, a retailer selling rats must give the buyer written or digital care instructions for the species at the time of sale (GBS §391-t), and keep copies on file.

Bringing a rat into New York from another state requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (CVI) issued within 30 days by a USDA-accredited vet (1CRR-NY 67.2). No rabies vaccine is required for rodents.
steps: Have a USDA-accredited vet issue a CVI within 30 days of entry

restrictions.summary: Keep rats in escape-proof caging — an escaped pet rat is legally indistinguishable from a feral pest under NYC's rodent-control rules (Art. 151), and harborage/active-rodent-signs carry fines. Never release a nonnative species.

inquiry_focus: We want to confirm New York treats a captive-bred Rattus rattus as a legal small companion animal (statewide 'unprotected wildlife' and NYC 'small rodent', not a banned 'large rodent' or prohibited wild animal), and whether the 30-day interstate import CVI (1CRR-NY 67.2) is enforced for a non-commercial private owner moving one pet rat.
